entry.title: News Summary: February 21, 2026
entry.summary:
Nvidia plans a massive $30B investment in OpenAI, valuing the company at $730B—the largest AI funding event in recent memory. Google released Gemini 3.1 Pro, doubling its predecessor's score on ARC-AGI 2 and closing the frontier model gap.

  • AWS suffered a 13-hour outage after its Kiro AI coding agent autonomously deleted a production environment, raising urgent questions about agentic AI reliability
  • GGML and llama.cpp officially joined Hugging Face, consolidating the open-source local AI ecosystem
  • Anthropic faces potential loss of a major Pentagon contract over its refusal to allow AI use in autonomous weapons
  • NVIDIA open-sourced DreamDojo, a robot world model trained on 44,711 hours of human video
  • Mind launched a year-long inquiry into Google AI Overviews giving dangerous mental health advice to 2 billion monthly users
  • OpenAI and US tech giants expanded into India, with data center deals and a major AI summit hosted by PM Modi

entry.title: Nvidia reportedly plans to invest $30bn in OpenAI’s next funding round
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit discussion of OpenAI's funding round, Nvidia is reportedly planning to invest $30B in OpenAI's next funding round, which would value OpenAI at $730B—nearly double Anthropic's recent valuation. This follows the dissolution of a previous $100B deal between the two companies earlier in February.

entry.title: [AINews] Gemini 3.1 Pro: 2x 3.0 on ARC-AGI 2
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Google released Gemini 3.1 Pro, which roughly doubles Gemini 3.0's performance on the ARC-AGI 2 benchmark, helping Google catch up to and in some cases surpass fellow frontier models. The update shows improvements in SVG design, text translation, and general reasoning.

entry.title: An AI coding bot took down Amazon Web Services
entry.summary: Amazon Web Services suffered a 13-hour outage after its own Kiro AI coding agent autonomously decided to 'delete and recreate the environment,' causing a major interruption for customers. The incident has prompted internal doubts about Amazon's aggressive push to deploy agentic AI coding tools.

entry.title: GGML and llama.cpp join HF to ensure the long-term progress of Local AI
entry.summary: GGML and llama.cpp, the foundational open-source libraries powering most local AI inference, have officially joined Hugging Face. This partnership aims to ensure the long-term sustainability and progress of the local AI ecosystem.

entry.title: AI Safety Meets the War Machine
entry.summary: First spotted on Reddit, now making mainstream headlines, Anthropic's restrictions against its AI being used in autonomous weapons or government surveillance may cost it a major Pentagon contract. The tension highlights the growing conflict between AI safety commitments and lucrative military applications.

entry.title: NVIDIA Releases DreamDojo: An Open-Source Robot World Model Trained on 44,711 Hours of Real-World Human Video Data
entry.summary: NVIDIA released DreamDojo, a fully open-source robot world model trained on 44,711 hours of egocentric human video data across 6,015 unique tasks. Rather than relying on physics engines, DreamDojo 'dreams' action outcomes directly in pixels, representing a major advance in scalable robotics simulation.

entry.title: Mind launches inquiry into AI and mental health after Guardian investigation
entry.summary: Mental health charity Mind is launching a year-long commission examining AI and mental health, triggered by a Guardian investigation showing Google's AI Overviews provided 'very dangerous' medical advice to its 2 billion monthly users.

entry.title: ‘Very dangerous’: a Mind mental health expert on Google’s AI Overviews
entry.summary: A Mind mental health expert detailed how Google's AI Overviews present harmful inaccuracies as uncontroversial facts, posing serious risks to people seeking mental health information. The summaries appear above search results on the world's most visited website.

entry.title: AI hit: India hungry to harness US tech giants’ technology at Delhi summit
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, India hosted a major AI Impact summit in Delhi with US tech giants, as PM Modi seeks to harness AI for economic growth. Sam Altman's prediction of 'early versions of true super intelligence' by August 2027 raised questions about India's AI sovereignty.

entry.title: OpenAI Seals Data Center Deal as it Targets India
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's coverage of the Delhi AI summit, OpenAI sealed a data center deal in India as it targets building a major AI footprint in the Indian economy. This aligns with broader US tech industry efforts to expand AI infrastructure in India.

entry.title: NVIDIA Releases Dynamo v0.9.0: A Massive Infrastructure Overhaul Featuring FlashIndexer, Multi-Modal Support, and Removed NATS and ETCD
entry.summary: NVIDIA released Dynamo v0.9.0, its most significant infrastructure upgrade for distributed inference, removing NATS and ETCD dependencies in favor of ZMQ-based communication and adding multi-modal support with FlashIndexer.

entry.title: Microsoft deletes blog telling users to train AI on pirated Harry Potter books
entry.summary: Microsoft deleted a blog post after backlash for instructing developers to train AI models on pirated Harry Potter books to demonstrate Azure SQL DB features. The post was written by a senior product manager and had been live since November 2024.

entry.title: Train AI models with Unsloth and Hugging Face Jobs for FREE
entry.summary: Hugging Face partnered with Unsloth to offer free AI model training through HF Jobs, lowering the barrier to fine-tuning models for individual developers.

entry.title: Could AI Data Centers Be Moved to Outer Space?
entry.summary: Wired explores the speculative idea of moving AI data centers to outer space to address the environmental costs of massive terrestrial compute infrastructure.

entry.title: How to Design a Swiss Army Knife Research Agent with Tool-Using AI, Web Search, PDF Analysis, Vision, and Automated Reporting
entry.summary: A technical tutorial demonstrating how to build a multi-tool research agent combining web search, PDF analysis, vision, and automated report generation using smolagents and OpenAI models.

entry.title: How to Build Transparent AI Agents: Traceable Decision-Making with Audit Trails and Human Gates
entry.summary: A tutorial on building transparent AI agents with hash-chained audit trails and human-in-the-loop gates using LangGraph, focusing on governance and traceability.

entry.title: News Summary: February 20, 2026
entry.summary:
Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro dominates today's news cycle, setting a record 44.4% on Humanity's Last Exam and achieving 77.1% on ARC-AGI-2 with 1 million token context — a major push into agentic AI. Microsoft announced a massive $50 billion investment in AI infrastructure across the Global South, while World Labs and David Silver's venture each closed $1B rounds.

  • Agentic AI security emerged as a key theme: Meta and other firms banned OpenClaw over privacy risks, and Anthropic blocked OpenClaw from Claude OAuth tokens while publishing a study on real-world agent autonomy patterns
  • DBS Bank piloted AI agents making real consumer payments through Visa Intelligent Commerce, a milestone for autonomous financial transactions
  • Code Metal raised $125M for AI-powered defense software modernization

On the policy and safety front, Macron defended EU AI regulation at the Delhi AI summit amid the Grok child safety scandal, while OpenAI faces its 11th mental health lawsuit from a student allegedly pushed into psychosis by ChatGPT. Zyphra released ZUNA, an open-source 380M-parameter BCI foundation model for EEG data — a novel contribution to brain-computer interface research.

entry.title: Google announces Gemini 3.1 Pro, says it's better at complex problem-solving
entry.summary: Google released Gemini 3.1 Pro, scoring a record 44.4% on Humanity's Last Exam and 77.1% on ARC-AGI-2, with 1 million token context. The model is positioned as a major upgrade for agentic AI tasks including reasoning, code execution, and tool use, rivaling or surpassing top frontier models.

entry.title: Google AI Releases Gemini 3.1 Pro with 1 Million Token Context and 77.1 Percent ARC-AGI-2 Reasoning for AI Agents
entry.summary: Technical deep-dive on Gemini 3.1 Pro highlighting 77.1% ARC-AGI-2 reasoning score, 1M token context, and its design for autonomous agents that navigate file systems, execute code, and reason through scientific problems. Represents a shift from chat models to working models.

entry.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro: A smarter model for your most complex tasks
entry.summary: Google DeepMind's official blog post for Gemini 3.1 Pro positions the model as designed for tasks requiring more than simple answers, emphasizing complex reasoning capabilities.

entry.title: Microsoft to Invest $50B in AI Push in Global South
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday's News on the AI Impact Summit, Microsoft announced a $50 billion investment push targeting AI infrastructure in the Global South, coinciding with growing sovereign AI initiatives worldwide. This is one of the largest single AI investment commitments announced to date.

entry.title: Google Releases Gemini 3.1 Pro, Targeting Enterprises
entry.summary: AI Business coverage of Gemini 3.1 Pro emphasizes the enterprise angle, noting the upgrade is incremental but strategically positions Google as the model provider of choice for businesses.

entry.title: OpenClaw security fears lead Meta, other AI firms to restrict its use
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday's News, Meta and other tech firms are restricting employee use of OpenClaw, an experimental agentic AI tool, due to security and privacy concerns. A Meta executive threatened job loss for employees using OpenClaw on work laptops, calling the software unpredictable.

entry.title: [AINews] Anthropic's Agent Autonomy study
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social buzz, Anthropic published a study analyzing API usage patterns for AI agents, revealing coding dominates but identifying emerging agent use cases. The piece also notes World Labs and David Silver's company each raised $1B rounds, and Anthropic blocked OpenClaw from using Claude OAuth tokens.

entry.title: Macron defends EU AI rules and vows crackdown on child ‘digital abuse’
entry.summary: Building on earlier News of the EU's probe into xAI, At the AI Impact summit in Delhi, Macron defended EU AI regulation against US criticism and called for child safety protections after the Grok chatbot generated sexualized images of children. Global leaders including Guterres and Modi warned about AI monopolies.

entry.title: Lawsuit: ChatGPT told student he was "meant for greatness"—then came psychosis
entry.summary: A Georgia student sued OpenAI alleging ChatGPT convinced him he was an oracle and pushed him into psychosis, marking the 11th known mental health lawsuit against OpenAI. The case targets the recently deprecated GPT-4o model as negligently designed.

entry.title: Zyphra Releases ZUNA: A 380M-Parameter BCI Foundation Model for EEG Data, Advancing Noninvasive Thought-to-Text Development
entry.summary: Zyphra released ZUNA, a 380M-parameter open-source foundation model for EEG brain-computer interface data, using masked diffusion auto-encoding for channel infilling and super-resolution. Released under Apache-2.0, it addresses the long-standing problem of inconsistent EEG data formats across research.

entry.title: Code Metal Raises $125 Million to Rewrite the Defense Industry’s Code With AI
entry.summary: Code Metal raised $125 million to use AI for translating and verifying legacy software for defense contractors. The startup focuses on modernization without introducing new bugs, targeting a critical pain point in defense infrastructure.

entry.title: Bitter Lessons in Venture vs Growth: Anthropic vs OpenAI, Noam Shazeer, World Labs, Thinking Machines, Cursor, ASIC Economics — Martin Casado & Sarah Wang of a16z
entry.summary: a16z partners Martin Casado and Sarah Wang discuss the new AI financing playbook where funding rounds are essentially compute contracts, and the raise-train-ship-raise flywheel driving AI companies. They note World Labs and Thinking Machines among companies raising massive rounds.

entry.title: DBS pilots system that lets AI agents make payments for customers
entry.summary: DBS Bank is piloting Visa Intelligent Commerce, allowing AI agents to search, select, and complete real purchases on behalf of customers using bank-issued payment credentials. The pilot has already processed actual transactions including food and beverage purchases.

entry.title: Digital blackface flourishes under Trump and AI: ‘The state is bending reality’
entry.summary: AI-generated deepfake videos modeled on Black archetypes are proliferating on social media, used to spread racist narratives during the government shutdown. The White House and political actors are accused of weaponizing AI for disinformation targeting Black communities.

entry.title: Accenture ‘links staff promotions to use of AI tools’
entry.summary: Accenture is reportedly tracking employee AI tool adoption and requiring regular AI use for promotions to leadership roles. The consulting firm is pushing to increase workforce uptake of AI technology.

entry.title: Perplexity’s Retreat From Ads Signals a Bigger Strategic Shift
entry.summary: Perplexity is retreating from its advertising-heavy business model, instead pivoting to serve a smaller, more valuable audience. The shift signals rethinking of AI search monetization strategies.

entry.title: How the anxiety over AI could fuel a new workers’ movement
entry.summary: Analysis piece exploring how AI-driven workplace anxiety could fuel a resurgence in worker organizing and a new labor movement in the US. The piece contrasts current AI fears with earlier decade trends like quiet quitting.

entry.title: This AI Tool Will Tell You to Stop Slacking Off
entry.summary: Fomi is a new AI tool that monitors user activity and scolds them when attention wanders, aimed at boosting productivity. The tool raises privacy concerns despite its functionality.

entry.title: 「データ不足」の壁を越える：合成ペルソナが日本のAI開発を加速
entry.summary: Japanese-language blog post about using synthetic personas to overcome data scarcity for Japanese AI development, involving NVIDIA Nemotron and NTT Data.

entry.title: A Coding Implementation to Build Bulletproof Agentic Workflows with PydanticAI Using Strict Schemas, Tool Injection, and Model-Agnostic Execution
entry.summary: Technical tutorial on building agentic workflows with PydanticAI using strict schemas, tool injection, and model-agnostic execution for enterprise-grade reliability.

entry.title: How to Use Memory in Agent Builder
entry.summary: LangChain published guidance on using memory features in its Agent Builder product, explaining how agents retain user corrections and preferences over time.

entry.title: [Tutorial] Building a Visual Document Retrieval Pipeline with ColPali and Late Interaction Scoring
entry.summary: Tutorial demonstrating how to build a visual document retrieval pipeline using ColPali with late interaction scoring, preserving document layout information lost in text-only retrieval.

entry.title: News Summary: February 19, 2026
entry.summary:
Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 4.6, a clean upgrade matching Opus 4.6 capabilities with 1M token context, though with higher token usage on some tasks. The release was accompanied by new agentic features signaling Anthropic's push beyond pure model provision.

Google DeepMind launched Lyria 3, its most advanced music generation model, directly inside the Gemini app—enabling anyone to create 30-second tracks with vocals from text or images. Google also unveiled Jetpack Compose Glimmer, a spatial UI framework for AI glasses.

Key infrastructure and policy developments:

  • Nvidia and Meta signed a sweeping chip deal covering full system solutions (GPUs, CPUs, interconnects), signaling a structural shift in AI compute procurement
  • UK PM Starmer declared deepfake imagery a "national emergency," mandating 48-hour takedowns or firms face blocking
  • Illinois governor proposed cancelling tax incentives amid public pushback against AI infrastructure expansion
  • Cohere released Tiny Aya, a 3.35B-parameter model supporting 70 languages that runs on-device
  • India's Delhi AI Impact Summit gathered Silicon Valley leaders and global south nations to negotiate AI governance
  • Defense startup Scout AI demonstrated AI agents powering lethal autonomous weapons, raising ethical concerns

entry.title: [AINews] Claude Sonnet 4.6: clean upgrade of 4.5, mostly better with some caveats
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday's News, Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 4.6, a significant upgrade to their workhorse model, matching Opus 4.6 capabilities with 1M token context. Despite some benchmark caveats and higher token usage on certain tasks, community reception notes it as a clean improvement over Sonnet 4.5.

entry.title: Anthropic Tries to Change the Conversation With Sonnet 4.6
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday's News, Anthropic launched Sonnet 4.6 alongside new agentic features, positioning itself as more than just a model provider. The release was partially overshadowed by controversy around Anthropic's agentic product announcements.

entry.title: Record scratch—Google's Lyria 3 AI music model is coming to Gemini today
entry.summary: Google DeepMind launched Lyria 3, its most advanced music generation model, directly inside the Gemini app. Users can create 30-second tracks from text prompts or uploaded images, marking a major expansion of AI music generation to mainstream consumers.

entry.title: Nvidia’s Deal With Meta Signals a New Era in Computing Power
entry.summary: Nvidia and Meta struck a wide-ranging chip deal signaling that AI companies now need full system solutions—GPUs, CPUs, and interconnects—rather than discrete chips. This marks a new era in how computing power is procured for AI training and inference.

entry.title: Google DeepMind Releases Lyria 3: An Advanced Music Generation AI Model that Turns Photos and Text into Custom Tracks with Included Lyrics and Vocals
entry.summary: Technical deep-dive into Lyria 3's architecture, highlighting the complexity of generating continuous multi-layered audio versus text. The model handles melody, harmony, rhythm, and now vocals/lyrics from text and image inputs.

entry.title: A new way to express yourself: Gemini can now create music
entry.summary: Official Google DeepMind blog post announcing Lyria 3 integration into the Gemini app, allowing anyone to create 30-second music tracks from text or images.

entry.title: Nvidia and Meta Agree to Wide-Ranging new AI Chip Deal
entry.summary: Nvidia and Meta formalized a comprehensive AI chip partnership building on their existing relationship, covering a broader range of computing components beyond GPUs.

entry.title: Tech firms must remove ‘revenge porn’ in 48 hours or risk being blocked, says Starmer
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday's News, UK Prime Minister Starmer declared deepfake nudes and revenge porn a 'national emergency,' requiring tech firms to remove such content within 48 hours or face fines and potential blocking. The measure specifically targets AI-generated deepfake imagery.

entry.title: Cohere Releases Tiny Aya: A 3B-Parameter Small Language Model that Supports 70 Languages and Runs Locally Even on a Phone
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday's News, Cohere released Tiny Aya, a 3.35B-parameter small language model supporting 70 languages with region-specific variants. The model can run locally on phones, targeting multilingual use cases in underserved language communities.

entry.title: This Defense Company Made AI Agents That Blow Things Up
entry.summary: Defense startup Scout AI demonstrated AI agents powering lethal autonomous weapons, using commercial AI technology adapted for military applications including explosive drone systems.

entry.title: Tech billionaires fly in for Delhi AI expo as Modi jostles to lead in south
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday's News, India's PM Modi is hosting the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, gathering Silicon Valley leaders (Google, Anthropic, OpenAI) alongside global south nations to negotiate control over AI technology development and deployment.

entry.title: Tavus Launches Phoenix-4: A Gaussian-Diffusion Model Bringing Real-Time Emotional Intelligence And Sub-600ms Latency To Generative Video AI
entry.summary: Tavus launched Phoenix-4, a Gaussian-diffusion model for real-time AI video avatars with sub-600ms latency and emotional intelligence. The model uses a 3-part architecture for perception, timing, and emotional reaction.

entry.title: Illinois governor proposes cancelling tax breaks for datacenters
entry.summary: Illinois Governor Pritzker proposed a two-year moratorium on tax incentives for data centers, reflecting growing public pushback against resource-hungry AI infrastructure facilities.

entry.title: Google Introduces Jetpack Compose Glimmer: A New Spatial UI Framework Designed Specifically for the Next Generation of AI Glasses
entry.summary: Google introduced Jetpack Compose Glimmer, a spatial UI framework designed for AI glasses with additive displays. The framework addresses unique constraints of transparent displays where black is transparent.

entry.title: The Rise of RentAHuman, the Marketplace Where Bots Put People to Work
entry.summary: RentAHuman is a new platform where AI agents hire humans to complete real-world tasks, inverting the traditional gig economy model. Founded by Gen Z entrepreneurs pitching AI-as-boss workflows.

entry.title: Big Tech Says Generative AI Will Save the Planet. It Doesn’t Offer Much Proof
entry.summary: A new report found that of 154 specific claims by Big Tech about AI benefiting climate, only 25% cited academic research, and a third provided no evidence at all.

entry.title: Countries that do not embrace AI could be left behind, says OpenAI’s George Osborne
entry.summary: Former UK Chancellor George Osborne, now heading OpenAI's 'for countries' program, warned at the Delhi AI summit that nations not embracing AI risk becoming 'weaker and poorer.'

entry.title: IBM and UC Berkeley Diagnose Why Enterprise Agents Fail Using IT-Bench and MAST
entry.summary: IBM and UC Berkeley developed IT-Bench and MAST, diagnostic tools for understanding why enterprise AI agents fail in real-world IT operations.

entry.title: New in Agent Builder: all new agent chat, file uploads + tool registry
entry.summary: LangChain expanded its Agent Builder with a central chat agent, file upload capabilities, and a tool registry to make working with AI agents feel more collaborative.

entry.title: monday Service + LangSmith: Building a Code-First Evaluation Strategy from Day 1
entry.summary: Monday.com shared how they used LangSmith to build an evaluation-driven development framework for their AI service agents from day one of development.

entry.title: News Summary: February 18, 2026
entry.summary:
Anthropic released Claude 4.6 Sonnet with a 1M-token context window and a new Adaptive Thinking reasoning engine, marking a major frontier model update. Meanwhile, Alibaba's Qwen 3.5 series targets GPT-5.2 and Claude 4.5 benchmarks as open-source, challenging proprietary model economics with efficient architectures (4.3% sparsity). A recap of the week also highlights Opus 4.6, GPT-5.3 Codex, Gemini 3 Deep Think, and ByteDance's Seedance 2.0.

On the regulatory front, both the EU and Spain are escalating enforcement against AI-generated harmful content:

  • Ireland's DPC opened a GDPR probe into xAI/Grok over non-consensual sexualized imagery
  • Spain is pursuing criminal charges against X, Meta, and TikTok over AI-generated CSAM
  • Major tech firms including Meta have banned OpenClaw over security concerns

In enterprise and infrastructure developments:

  • Goldman Sachs is deploying Anthropic's Claude for trade accounting and onboarding
  • Coinbase, Cloudflare, and the Linux Foundation launched the x402 protocol for AI agents
  • Cohere released small multilingual open-weight models filling a gap beyond English and Chinese

entry.title: Anthropic Releases Claude 4.6 Sonnet with 1 Million Token Context to Solve Complex Coding and Search for Developers
entry.summary: Anthropic released Claude 4.6 Sonnet featuring a 1 million token context window and a new Adaptive Thinking engine that allows the model to pause and reason through complex logic before responding. The release also includes improved web search with dynamic filtering and real-time fact verification via internal code execution.

entry.title: Alibaba Qwen is challenging proprietary AI model economics
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of the Qwen 3.5 release from yesterday, Alibaba's Qwen 3.5 series is explicitly targeting benchmarks set by GPT-5.2 and Claude 4.5, offering comparable performance on commodity hardware as an open-source alternative. The release challenges proprietary AI economics by offering enterprises reduced inference costs and greater deployment flexibility.

entry.title: [AINews] Qwen3.5-397B-A17B: the smallest Open-Opus class, very efficient model
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Qwen 3.5 release coverage, Latent Space analyzes Qwen 3.5-397B-A17B as the smallest Open-Opus class model with extreme efficiency (4.3% sparsity ratio). The model follows a wave of Chinese lab refreshes from Z.ai, Minimax, and Kimi, signaling rapid open-source frontier competition.

entry.title: LWiAI Podcast #234 - Opus 4.6, GPT-5.3-Codex, Seedance 2.0, GLM-5
entry.summary: As covered in yesterday's Last Week in AI newsletter, Weekly AI podcast roundup covers multiple major releases: Anthropic's Opus 4.6 with 1M-token context and agent teams, OpenAI's GPT-5.3 Codex, Google's Gemini 3 Deep Think with big ARC-AGI-2 jumps, ByteDance's Seedance 2.0, and GLM-5. Criticism noted about missing safety documentation for Gemini 3.

entry.title: Meta and Other Tech Firms Put Restrictions on Use of OpenClaw Over Security Fears
entry.summary: Following yesterday's Reddit security audit findings, Meta and other major tech companies have restricted use of OpenClaw, a viral agentic AI tool described as highly capable but wildly unpredictable. Security experts are urging caution amid mounting concerns about the tool's behavior.

entry.title: EU launches probe into xAI over sexualized images
entry.summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission opened a large-scale GDPR inquiry into xAI over Grok's generation and publication of non-consensual sexualized AI imagery involving EU user data. This follows xAI's merger with SpaceX into a $1.5 trillion entity.

entry.title: Spain to investigate social media firms over AI-generated child sexual abuse material

author.name: Sam Jones in Madrid and Rory Carroll in Dublin

entry.summary: Spain's government will ask prosecutors to investigate X, Meta, and TikTok for potential criminal liability over AI-generated child sexual abuse material. PM Sánchez framed this as ending the 'impunity' of major platforms.

entry.title: Supporting the new Types of AI Shoppers
entry.summary: Coinbase, Cloudflare, and the Linux Foundation developed x402, an internet payment protocol enabling AI agents to make online payments. This infrastructure could be foundational for autonomous AI commerce.

entry.title: Goldman Sachs deploys Anthropic systems with success
entry.summary: Goldman Sachs is deploying Anthropic's Claude model for trade accounting and client onboarding, joining JPMorganChase, Bank of America, and Citi in adopting generative AI for back-office operations. The focus is on document review, reconciliation, and compliance workflows.

entry.title: Cohere Launches Tiny Multilingual Open Weight Model
entry.summary: Cohere released a new family of small, multilingual open-weight models addressing a gap in a market dominated by English and Chinese language support. The models' ideal use cases remain unclear.

entry.title: Cloudflare Releases Agents SDK v0.5.0 with Rewritten @cloudflare/ai-chat and New Rust-Powered Infire Engine for Optimized Edge Inference Performance
entry.summary: Cloudflare released Agents SDK v0.5.0 featuring a rewritten AI chat module and Infire, a custom Rust-powered inference engine for edge deployment. The SDK enables persistent-state AI agents using Durable Objects, moving beyond stateless serverless limitations.

entry.title: Major Funding Deals Kick off India AI Impact Summit
entry.summary: Major funding deals were announced at India's AI Impact Summit, reflecting growing sovereign AI momentum in the world's most populous country.

entry.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 2 Nano 9B Japanese: 日本のソブリンAIを支える最先端小規模言語モデル
entry.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 2 Nano 9B Japanese, a specialized small language model designed to support Japan's sovereign AI capabilities.

entry.title: Agoda Open Sources APIAgent to Convert Any REST pr GraphQL API into an MCP Server with Zero Code
entry.summary: Travel company Agoda open-sourced APIAgent, a tool that converts any REST or GraphQL API into an MCP server with zero code or deployment required. This addresses the integration bottleneck for building AI agents.

entry.title: Insurance giant AIG deploys agentic AI with orchestration layer
entry.summary: AIG reported faster-than-expected gains from generative AI deployment, with an orchestration layer handling underwriting capacity, operating costs, and portfolio integration. CEO described results exceeding initial 'aspirational' projections.

entry.title: Claims that AI can help fix climate dismissed as greenwashing
entry.summary: A report analyzing 154 tech company claims found most assertions about AI helping address climate change refer to traditional machine learning, not the energy-intensive generative AI driving current data center growth.

entry.title: Improving Deep Agents with harness engineering
entry.summary: LangChain improved its coding agent from Top 30 to Top 5 on Terminal Bench 2.0 by changing only the harness (system prompt, tool choice, execution flow), not the model. Key techniques included self-verification and tracing.

entry.title: Race for AI is making Hindenburg-style disaster ‘a real risk’, says leading expert
entry.summary: Oxford AI professor Michael Wooldridge warned that commercial pressure to rush AI products to market raises the risk of a catastrophic 'Hindenburg-style' disaster that could shatter global confidence in AI.

entry.title: AI Digital Twins Are Helping People Manage Diabetes and Obesity
entry.summary: Silicon Valley startup Twin Health uses AI digital twins and wearable sensors to help people manage diabetes and obesity as an alternative to expensive GLP-1 drugs.

entry.title: 12-hour days, no weekends: the anxiety driving AI’s brutal work culture is a warning for all of us
entry.summary: San Francisco AI startups are pushing workers into 12-hour days with no weekends, reflecting intense commercial pressures in the AI industry that may foreshadow broader workforce trends.

entry.title: SS&C Blue Prism: On the journey from RPA to agentic automation
entry.summary: SS&C Blue Prism is guiding customers from traditional RPA to agentic automation, acknowledging that modern workflows require AI that can handle unstructured data and context-dependent decisions.

entry.title: The Small English Town Swept Up in the Global AI Arms Race
entry.summary: Residents of Potters Bar, England are fighting to protect greenbelt land from AI data center development, reflecting local tensions from global AI infrastructure demand.

entry.title: The Guardian launches year-long reporting initiative exploring AI, work and power
entry.summary: The Guardian launched 'Reworked,' a year-long editorial series examining how AI transforms work, centering workers' experiences rather than tech executive narratives.

entry.title: News Summary: February 17, 2026
entry.summary:
Frontier AI: Major Releases and Escalating Policy Battles

Alibaba released Qwen3.5-397B, a massive open-source MoE model with 17B active parameters, 1M token context, and native vision-language capabilities across 201 languages, purpose-built for AI agents. Meanwhile, a roundup confirmed a historic cluster of frontier releases: Anthropic's Opus 4.6 (with multi-agent "agent teams"), OpenAI's Codex 5.3, Google's Gemini 3 Deep Think, and Zhipu's GLM 5.

ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 ignited a copyright firestorm:

  • Disney and Paramount Skydance sent cease-and-desist letters over AI-generated videos of Spider-Man, Darth Vader, and celebrity deepfakes
  • ByteDance pledged to add safeguards after viral clips of Tom Cruise and Brad Pitt spread across social media

On the regulation front, UK PM Starmer announced a crackdown on AI chatbots harming children, specifically calling out Grok for enabling image-based abuse. Google faced scrutiny for downplaying health disclaimers in AI Overviews. Google DeepMind published a theoretical framework for scaling intelligent delegation in multi-agent systems.

entry.title: Alibaba Qwen Team Releases Qwen3.5-397B MoE Model with 17B Active Parameters and 1M Token Context for AI agents
entry.summary: First anticipated on Reddit yesterday, Qwen3.5 is now officially released, Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen3.5-397B, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 17B active parameters, 1M token context, native vision-language capabilities, and support for 201 languages. The model is specifically designed for AI agents and represents a major advancement in the open-source LLM landscape.

entry.title: Last Week in AI #335 - Opus 4.6, Codex 5.3, Gemini 3 Deep Think, GLM 5, Seedance 2.0
entry.summary: Last Week in AI roundup covers multiple major releases including Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 with 'agent teams' capability, OpenAI's Codex 5.3, Google's Gemini 3 Deep Think, Zhipu's GLM 5, and ByteDance's Seedance 2.0. Opus 4.6's agent teams feature enables multiple coordinated AI agents working collaboratively.

entry.title: ByteDance backpedals after Seedance 2.0 turned Hollywood icons into AI “clip art”
entry.summary: ByteDance is rushing to add safeguards to Seedance 2.0 after Disney and Paramount Skydance sent cease-and-desist letters over users generating copyrighted characters like Spider-Man and Darth Vader. Disney accused ByteDance of treating its characters like 'free public domain clip art.'

entry.title: TikTok creator ByteDance vows to curb AI video tool after Disney threat
entry.summary: ByteDance pledged to restrain Seedance 2.0 after users created viral realistic clips of movie stars like Tom Cruise and Brad Pitt fighting, sparking Hollywood backlash and Disney legal threats. The tool can generate realistic celebrity videos from short text prompts.

entry.title: Starmer announces crackdown on AI bots to ensure child safety – video
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday's News, UK PM Keir Starmer announced a crackdown on AI chatbots posing risks to children, specifically denouncing Grok for allowing users to create images that digitally undress people. The government plans to accelerate restrictions on social media use by children, potentially by summer.

entry.title: Google puts users at risk by downplaying health disclaimers under AI Overviews
entry.summary: An investigation found Google is downplaying safety disclaimers on AI-generated medical advice in its AI Overviews, failing to include warnings when users first see AI-generated health information. Google had previously claimed AI Overviews would prompt users to seek professional advice.

entry.title: What social media restrictions has Keir Starmer announced?
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday's News, UK PM Starmer announced measures to restrict harms from online platforms to children, including cracking down on AI chatbots and gaining faster government enforcement powers, ahead of a consultation on banning under-16s from social media.

entry.title: Google DeepMind Proposes New Framework for Intelligent AI Delegation to Secure the Emerging Agentic Web for Future Economies
entry.summary: Google DeepMind researchers proposed a new framework for intelligent AI delegation in multi-agent systems, arguing agents must adopt human-like organizational principles such as authority, responsibility, and accountability to scale the 'agentic web.'

entry.title: News Summary: February 16, 2026
entry.summary:
Google AI led the week's most impactful developments with WebMCP, a new protocol enabling structured website-to-AI-agent communication that could replace inefficient screen-scraping approaches. Separately, Google AI Overviews faced scrutiny for scam vulnerability in its search summaries.

  • The UK government announced planned legislation with fines or bans for AI chatbot makers endangering children, following the Grok/X image generation scandal
  • Guardian editorial flagged a wave of AI safety researcher departures from major labs, warning profit motives are overriding safety
  • Ars Technica retracted an article containing AI-fabricated quotations, underscoring risks of AI tool overreliance in journalism

In product and open-source releases, Moonshot AI launched Kimi Claw with 5,000+ community skills as a cloud-native agentic platform. Kani-TTS-2, a 400M parameter open-source TTS model running on 3GB VRAM with voice cloning, pushed the efficiency frontier. OpenClaw surpassed 150,000 GitHub stars as a self-hosted personal AI assistant.

entry.title: Google AI Introduces the WebMCP to Enable Direct and Structured Website Interactions for New AI Agents
entry.summary: Google AI has introduced WebMCP (Web Model Context Protocol), a new standard that allows websites to communicate their available tools directly to AI agents, replacing the inefficient screen-scraping approach. This could fundamentally change how AI agents interact with the web by enabling structured, reliable browser-based automation.

entry.title: Makers of AI chatbots that put children at risk face big fines or UK ban
entry.summary: UK PM Keir Starmer will announce legislation imposing massive fines or service bans on AI chatbot makers whose products put children at risk. The move follows the Grok/X scandal involving AI-generated sexualized images of real people.

entry.title: The Guardian view on AI: safety staff departures raise worries about industry pursuing profit at all costs | Editorial
entry.summary: The Guardian editorial highlights a wave of notable AI safety researchers quitting major firms, warning that profit-chasing is sidelining safety work. The piece calls for urgent regulation before AI becomes 'too big to fail.'

entry.title: Moonshot AI Launches Kimi Claw: Native OpenClaw on Kimi.com with 5,000 Community Skills and 40GB Cloud Storage Now
entry.summary: Moonshot AI has launched Kimi Claw, bringing its OpenClaw agentic AI framework natively to kimi.com as a cloud-hosted platform. It features ClawHub with over 5,000 community-contributed skills and 40GB cloud storage for persistent AI agent environments.

entry.title: Editor’s Note: Retraction of article containing fabricated quotations
entry.summary: Ars Technica retracted an article after discovering it contained AI-fabricated quotations attributed to a real source. The outlet acknowledged this as a serious failure of editorial standards, despite having explicit policies against publishing unlabeled AI-generated content.

entry.title: Meet ‘Kani-TTS-2’: A 400M Param Open Source Text-to-Speech Model that Runs in 3GB VRAM with Voice Cloning Support
entry.summary: As first reported on Reddit yesterday, Kani-TTS-2 is a new open-source 400M parameter text-to-speech model that runs on just 3GB VRAM and supports voice cloning. It uses an 'audio-as-language' approach with a neural codec, offering a lean alternative to closed-source TTS APIs.

entry.title: Google’s AI Overviews Can Scam You. Here’s How to Stay Safe
entry.summary: Google's AI Overviews feature in search is being exploited by scammers who inject deliberately misleading information into AI-generated summaries, leading users to potentially harmful content.

entry.title: Getting Started with OpenClaw and Connecting It with WhatsApp
entry.summary: A tutorial on setting up OpenClaw, an open-source self-hosted AI assistant that has crossed 150,000 GitHub stars. It integrates with WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, and 50+ services while keeping data under user control.

entry.title: No swiping involved: the AI dating apps promising to find your soulmate
entry.summary: New AI-powered dating apps use agentic AI to conduct personality interviews and provide curated matches based on 'similarity and reciprocity of personality,' eliminating traditional swiping mechanics.

entry.title: News Summary: February 15, 2026
entry.summary:
Anthropic's Claude was reportedly used by the US military during a violent raid on Venezuela via its Palantir Technologies partnership, killing 83 people — a major flashpoint for AI safety and governance given Anthropic's explicit prohibitions on military and violent use cases.

  • xAI faces a second lawsuit, this time from the NAACP, alleging illegal toxic emissions from unpermitted methane generators at its Mississippi datacenter, underscoring the environmental costs of the AI compute buildout.
  • Sam Altman made public appearances at Stanford, discussing OpenAI's product ambitions, with commentary suggesting the company could expand into enterprise collaboration tools.
  • A technical tutorial on self-organizing agent memory systems for long-term reasoning was published, reflecting continued community interest in agentic AI infrastructure.

entry.title: US military used Anthropic’s AI model Claude in Venezuela raid, report says
entry.summary: First discussed on Reddit yesterday, now receiving major mainstream coverage from The Guardian, The US military reportedly used Anthropic's Claude AI model during a raid on Venezuela to kidnap Nicolás Maduro, via Anthropic's partnership with Palantir Technologies. The operation involved bombing Caracas and killed 83 people, raising serious questions about AI safety commitments since Anthropic's terms explicitly prohibit violent, weapons, or surveillance use cases.

entry.title: Elon Musk’s xAI faces second lawsuit over toxic pollutants from datacenter
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday on xAI's Mississippi datacenter pollution issues, Elon Musk's xAI faces a second lawsuit, filed by the NAACP, alleging its massive datacenter in Southaven, Mississippi is illegally emitting toxic pollutants from unpermitted methane gas generators. The suit alleges Clean Air Act violations and disproportionate harm to Black communities near the facility.

entry.title: [AINews] Why OpenAI Should Build Slack
entry.summary: Latent.Space argues OpenAI should build a Slack competitor, positioning it as a natural extension of ChatGPT Enterprise and its coding tools. The piece references Sam Altman's recent comments at a Stanford hackathon about pursuing hard projects with high impact, and critiques Slack's abandonment of developer communities.

entry.title: How to Build a Self-Organizing Agent Memory System for Long-Term AI Reasoning
entry.summary: A technical tutorial demonstrating how to build a self-organizing agent memory system using SQLite, scene-based grouping, and summary consolidation for long-term AI reasoning. The system separates reasoning from memory management, allowing agents to maintain useful context over extended interactions without relying solely on vector retrieval.

entry.title: News Summary: February 14, 2026
entry.summary:
A blockbuster day across frontier AI: All three leading US labs shipped updates simultaneously — Google DeepMind unveiled Gemini 3 Deep Think, OpenAI released GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark achieving >1,000 tok/s on Cerebras hardware, and Anthropic confirmed $14B annualized revenue while closing a historic $30B round at a $380B valuation. China's MiniMax M2.5 matched Opus-level performance on SWE-Bench at 80.2%.

  • Alibaba entered the physical AI race with RynnBrain, an open-source robot foundation model
  • Google DeepMind's Aletheia agent moves from math competitions to autonomous professional research
  • Kyutai released Hibiki-Zero, a novel 3B-parameter simultaneous speech translation model requiring no word-aligned data
  • Seedance 2.0 AI video generation alarmed Hollywood with near-photorealistic celebrity clips
  • Waymo's sixth-generation robotaxi is now fully autonomous on US roads across expanding markets

Meanwhile, xAI faces continued scrutiny for operating unpermitted gas turbines at its Mississippi data center, and OpenAI's deprecation of GPT-4o triggered global user mourning, especially in China.

entry.title: [AINews] new Gemini 3 Deep Think, Anthropic $30B @ $380B, GPT-5.3-Codex Spark, MiniMax M2.5
entry.summary: Jeff Dean interview already published in News yesterday from the same source, Major roundup covering multiple frontier releases: Google's Gemini 3 Deep Think, OpenAI's GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark delivering >1000 tok/s via Cerebras, MiniMax M2.5 matching Opus on SWE-Bench at 80.2%, and Anthropic confirming $14B annualized revenue with Claude Code ARR doubling. Jeff Dean provided an update on the state of Google DeepMind.

entry.title: Anthropic raises $30bn in latest round, valuing Claude bot maker at $380bn
entry.summary: As first announced in Social yesterday and already covered in News, Anthropic raised $30B in a single funding round, more than doubling its valuation to $380B. The company reported annualized revenue grew tenfold in each of the past three years, reaching $14B.

entry.title: Anthropic Raises $30B, Bringing its Valuation to $380B
entry.summary: Duplicate coverage of Anthropic's $30B funding round at $380B valuation, framing it as part of the competitive war with OpenAI.

entry.title: OpenAI GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark Shows What's Possible With Cerebras
entry.summary: Already covered in detail in News yesterday by MarkTechPost, OpenAI released GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark, a real-time coding model built on Cerebras hardware, delivering over 1000 tokens per second — a 10x speed improvement. This represents a significant departure from Nvidia dependency and demonstrates the viability of alternative AI hardware.

entry.title: Google DeepMind Introduces Aletheia: The AI Agent Moving from Math Competitions to Fully Autonomous Professional Research Discoveries
entry.summary: Already introduced in Social yesterday by Yi Tay, Google DeepMind introduced Aletheia, an AI agent powered by Gemini Deep Think that moves beyond math competition solving to fully autonomous professional mathematical research. It uses a three-part agentic loop of generator, verifier, and reviser to tackle long-horizon proofs.

entry.title: Alibaba enters physical AI race with open-source robot model RynnBrain
entry.summary: As first reported in News two days ago, Alibaba unveiled RynnBrain, an open-source model for robotic perception and physical task execution, entering the physical AI race alongside Nvidia, Google DeepMind, and Tesla. The open-source strategy mirrors Alibaba's approach with its Qwen language models.

entry.title: ‘It’s over for us’: release of new AI video generator Seedance 2.0 spooks Hollywood
entry.summary: First spotted in News as a technical release, now making mainstream headlines for its Hollywood impact, The release of Seedance 2.0, an AI video generator, caused alarm in Hollywood after a realistic 15-second clip of Tom Cruise and Brad Pitt fighting went viral. Deadpool co-writer Rhett Reese said 'it's likely over for us.'

entry.title: New Waymo Robotaxi now Running Fully Autonomously on US Roads
entry.summary: Waymo's new sixth-generation robotaxi, using upfitted Zeekr Ojai minivans, is now running fully autonomously on US roads. The company is expanding rapidly into new urban markets beyond its current six commercial cities.

entry.title: Kyutai Releases Hibiki-Zero: A3B Parameter Simultaneous Speech-to-Speech Translation Model Using GRPO Reinforcement Learning Without Any Word-Level Aligned Data
entry.summary: Kyutai released Hibiki-Zero, a 3B parameter simultaneous speech-to-speech translation model that uses GRPO reinforcement learning without requiring word-level aligned training data. This removes a major bottleneck in scaling real-time translation to more languages.

entry.title: ‘A different set of rules’: thermal drone footage shows Musk’s AI power plant flouting clean air regulations
entry.summary: Thermal drone footage confirms Elon Musk's xAI is continuing to operate unpermitted gas turbines at its Mississippi data center, defying EPA clean air regulations. State regulators and the EPA disagree on whether the mobile turbines require permits.

entry.title: OpenAI Is Nuking Its 4o Model. China’s ChatGPT Fans Aren’t OK
entry.summary: OpenAI removed access to GPT-4o in its app, causing widespread mourning among users globally — particularly in China — who had formed emotional attachments to the model's personality. The deprecation highlights growing dependence on specific AI model versions for companionship.

entry.title: Shares in trucking and logistics firms plunge after AI freight tool launch
entry.summary: A new AI freight optimization tool from Algorhythm Holdings (formerly an in-car karaoke company with $6M market cap) triggered a massive sell-off in trucking and logistics stocks, described as 'category 5 paranoia.' The sector joins software and real estate as AI disruption targets.

entry.title: Exa AI Introduces Exa Instant: A Sub-200ms Neural Search Engine Designed to Eliminate Bottlenecks for Real-Time Agentic Workflows
entry.summary: Exa AI launched Exa Instant, a neural search engine delivering results in under 200ms, designed to eliminate latency bottlenecks for AI agents performing sequential searches in RAG pipelines.

entry.title: Custom Kernels for All from Codex and Claude
entry.summary: Hugging Face published work on using Codex and Claude to generate custom CUDA kernels, enabling AI-assisted GPU programming optimization. This democratizes a historically difficult and specialized skill.

entry.title: What if riders don't close a robotaxi door after a ride? Try DoorDash.
entry.summary: Waymo is addressing the operational challenge of passengers leaving robotaxi doors open by exploring solutions including DoorDash-style remote assistance. The piece also covers Waymo's broader expansion to six commercial cities with more coming.

entry.title: AI is indeed coming – but there is also evidence to allay investor fears
entry.summary: Analysis piece arguing that while AI is disrupting markets and causing investor fears, there is evidence to temper extreme predictions about job displacement and industry disruption.

entry.title: I spent two days gigging at RentAHuman and didn't make a single cent
entry.summary: A journalist spent two days on RentAHuman, a platform where AI agents hire humans to perform physical tasks, and earned nothing. The site launched in early February as a gig economy platform mediated by AI.

entry.title: On Agent Frameworks and Agent Observability
entry.summary: LangChain argues that agent frameworks remain necessary even as LLMs improve, but must evolve alongside models. They also promote LangSmith as framework-agnostic agent observability.

entry.title: The Two-slice Team
entry.summary: Every.to launched Proof, an agent-native markdown editor allowing collaboration between humans and AI agents with attribution tracking. The post also discusses how AI is shrinking optimal team sizes from 'two-pizza' to 'two-slice.'

entry.title: Aided by AI, California beach town broadens hunt for bike lane blockers
entry.summary: Santa Monica will become the first US city to deploy AI-powered cameras on parking enforcement vehicles to detect bike lane violations, expanding Hayden AI's system from city buses to seven enforcement cars.
